chapter: Politics, Africa, religion and the Paris conversion
title: What reading the Psalms did to her
summary: She says the Psalms uprooted her and freed her from being stuck, a magic that you have to experience.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: One thing I don't understand. Reading all the Psalms, what did that do to you?

You know what that did? I discovered I was stuck and it uprooted me like it would a tree when a storm hit it and moved me on to things I was supposed to be doing. I wasn't supposed to be there because the last two months I hadn't worked at all. I was finished in England until a later date. You know, you can stay too long. In Europe if you go there, when you go in fresh you get maybe $100 a night but if you keep staying it gets smaller and smaller. I just couldn't get away.
How did reading the Psalms unstick you?
Have you ever read the Psalms? Any of them?
But I never read all of them.
What effect did it have on you. Did it make you get up and move, was that the idea?

You're crying out so for God's help till you shed everything, everything that's holding you back. You see, sometimes we can get hung up in a situation and can't get out. You know, it's just like a magnet; it keeps holding you. Sometimes we can get out too soon. We don't let it worry us but some things can just drag and drag and drag. You feel, I'm finished here. Like, I've been in a night club. They'd want to held me over and I'd say no, I'm gone. Because until a later date, because you peter out, see, completely. So that's what I felt. But what this does - you have to do it to find out. But it's magic.
